back: Stereoisomers in which two identical ligands are adjacent (cis, 90°) or opposite (trans, 180°).
Square planar MA₂B₂ (e.g. [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂]) and octahedral MA₄B₂ (e.g. [Co(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺); not tetrahedral complexes.
cis-[Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂], square planar Pt(II); an anticancer drug. The trans isomer is not used clinically.
In cells, water replaces the Cl⁻ ligands; Pt binds to two adjacent guanine bases on DNA, which stops replication.
Octahedral complexes with three bidentate ligands ([Ni(en)₃]²⁺) or the cis form of M(AA)₂B₂ (cis-[Ni(en)₂(H₂O)₂]²⁺).
Three: trans (plane of symmetry, not chiral) and a pair of cis enantiomers.
Cis isomers are polar; in trans isomers equal bond dipoles are opposite and cancel.
The donor atoms are joined by a short chain, so they can only reach adjacent positions (90°).
